chunks: Abd al-Wahid b. Muhammad al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Muhammad b. Qutayba al-Nisapuri narrated to us. He said: Hamdan b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Nu'man narrated to us from Abdullah b. Talha from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever fasts the twenty-seventh of Rajab, Allah records the reward of seventy years of fasting for him.

key_terms.أجر: Reward (ajr): divine recompense for good deeds in the hereafter
key_terms.رجب: Rajab: the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar, one of the four sacred months
key_terms.صام: Fasted (sawm/siyam): the Islamic practice of abstaining from food, drink, and other needs from dawn to sunset

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the 27th of Rajab in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) highlights the immense spiritual reward of fasting on the twenty-seventh of Rajab, stating that Allah records the equivalent of seventy years of fasting for one who observes this fast. This hadith, delivered in the assembly of Rajab 368 AH, underscores the special merit that the sacred month of Rajab holds in the Shia tradition, where specific days carry multiplied rewards as an encouragement to increase worship during sacred times.
